domain_label: DTC Plated-Jewelry Viability — CAC, AOV, LTV, Payback, Break-Even & Go/No-Go
purpose: A decision method for judging whether a paid-social DTC launch of plated fashion-jewelry accessories can be viable, by comparing an inherited per-order contribution margin against paid-social CAC on first-order economics, LTV:CAC and CAC-payback, deriving break-even units and break-even ROAS from the cost+price stack, sequencing the launch test budget, and firing pre-committed honest kill-criteria — while treating every actual CAC / repeat-rate / return-rate number as [UNKNOWN until measured] with a stated [METHOD], never a guess.
assumptions: the per-unit landed COGS and defensible retail price are inherited as labelled inputs from kb1_cogs_and_landed and kb2_pricing_and_margin; this KB does not re-derive them, it runs viability arithmetic on top of them [METHOD-inherited]

contribution margin = price - variable cost per unit (landed COGS + payment/processing fee + pick-pack + variable shipping + expected return cost) [FACT-managerial accounting]; only variable costs enter, fixed costs enter break-even not contribution

actual CAC, purchase frequency, repeat rate, AOV and return rate for the owner's audience are genuinely [UNKNOWN] until the store and paid campaigns generate first-party data; benchmarks are carried as [ESTIMATE] with method+confidence, never as measured facts

the LTV:CAC >= 3:1 and CAC-payback < 12-month rules of thumb are venture/SaaS heuristics [FACT-heuristic, with caveats], not laws; they are used as screening bands and always paired with first-order cash economics for a low-repeat impulse-accessory category
post-iOS-14.5 ATT attribution loss makes platform-reported CAC/ROAS optimistic; blended (all-in) CAC and holdout/MER reads are the honest denominators [FACT-attribution degradation]

every claim is tagged [FACT] (with basis), [ESTIMATE] (with method+confidence), [METHOD] (a way to obtain the number), or [UNKNOWN]; no market size, purchase rate, competitor price, or CAC figure is invented
exclusions: re-deriving landed COGS (kb1_cogs_and_landed owns it) or the retail price and contribution-margin construction (kb2_pricing_and_margin owns it); this KB accepts them as input
the demand read, category/finish sizing, consumer segmentation and competitor mapping (the jewel_market specialist owns those); this KB does not estimate market size or who buys
the poll/survey instrument design and paid-poll signal extraction (the jewel_poll specialist owns those); this KB uses the launch as the CAC/AOV experiment, not the preference poll
the final 6-SKU launch assortment selection and keep/cut sell-through protocol (the jewel_assortment specialist owns those); this KB hands it a viability verdict and budget plan, not a SKU list
tax, securities, accounting or fundraising advice; this models unit-economics viability and a launch-budget decision procedure, not a financial statement or a raise

competency_questions.question: What per-order contribution does the launch actually earn, given accessory AOV and units-per-order, and where does it come from?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTRIBUTION_INPUT states the inherited price-minus-variable-cost contribution per unit, AOV_BASKET states how to estimate accessory AOV and units-per-order and why accessory baskets are low-AOV, and CONTRIBUTION_PER_ORDER composes them into contribution-per-order net of order-level variable costs

competency_questions.question: How is CAC via paid IG/TikTok/Meta measured rather than guessed, and what funnel drives it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAC_PAID_SOCIAL states CAC = ad spend / new customers, decomposes it through the CPM -> CTR -> LP conversion-rate funnel, and flags CAC as [UNKNOWN until measured] with benchmarks only [ESTIMATE] and platform-reported CAC optimistic post-ATT

competency_questions.question: Why must blended/marginal CAC, not platform-reported CAC, be the denominator for a viability verdict?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BLENDED_VS_PAID_CAC distinguishes blended (all spend / all new customers) from paid marginal CAC and platform-attributed CAC, and states that organic dilution flatters blended CAC while ATT flatters platform CAC, so scaling decisions steer on marginal paid CAC and holdout/MER

competency_questions.question: Does the launch make money on the first order, and why does first-order economics gate a cash-thin DTC?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FIRST_ORDER_ECONOMICS computes first-order profit = contribution-per-order - CAC and states that for a low-repeat impulse accessory a business that loses money on order one is betting the whole model on an [UNKNOWN] repeat rate

competency_questions.question: How is LTV built honestly for fashion accessories given an unknown repeat rate, and why is it a gross-margin cohort number not a revenue number?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPEAT_RATE_LTV states repeat/frequency for accessories is [UNKNOWN] and gives the cohort [METHOD], and LTV_MODEL builds LTV = contribution-per-order x expected orders-per-customer (discounted), never revenue x a made-up multiple

competency_questions.question: What does the LTV:CAC ratio test actually tell you, and where does the 3:1 rule of thumb mislead for impulse accessories?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAC_LTV_RATIO states LTV:CAC using contribution LTV over marginal CAC, presents >=3:1 as a [FACT-heuristic] screening band, and flags that a low-repeat category can pass a ratio built on an optimistic repeat assumption while failing on cash, so the ratio never stands alone

competency_questions.question: What is the CAC payback period and why does payback matter more than the ratio for a self-funded launch?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PAYBACK_PERIOD defines payback = CAC / contribution-per-period (or orders-to-recover CAC), states the < ~12-month / recover-within-first-order-or-two screening band [FACT-heuristic], and explains that payback governs the working-capital cash cycle a bootstrapped DTC lives or dies on

competency_questions.question: How many units and what ROAS/MER must the launch hit to break even, computed from the cost+price stack?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BREAK_EVEN_UNITS computes break-even units = fixed+launch costs / contribution-per-unit and CAC-inclusive break-even, and BREAK_EVEN_ROAS derives break-even ROAS ~= 1 / contribution-margin-ratio and the break-even MER threshold below which paid spend loses money

competency_questions.question: How do returns, refunds and shipping subsidies leak contribution, and how are they carried without double-counting?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETURNS_DRAG states return/refund/chargeback cost as a [UNKNOWN]-rate deduction from contribution via net-of-returns contribution, and SHIPPING_FREE_THRESHOLD states the free-shipping threshold vs AOV trade and how a subsidy erodes contribution while a threshold lifts AOV

competency_questions.question: How is the launch test budget sequenced, and why does CAC rise as spend scales?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LAUNCH_BUDGET_SEQUENCING states a staged test budget (per-SKU learning-phase spend, gates before scaling) with a pre-committed learning budget treated as tuition, and COHORT_SCALING_CAC_CURVE states that marginal CAC rises with spend as the audience saturates and CPM climbs, so early cheap CAC does not extrapolate

competency_questions.question: Which input is the viability verdict most fragile to, and how is that stress-tested before committing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SENSITIVITY_STRESS ranks the verdict's fragility across CAC, repeat rate, AOV and return rate, and states that a verdict resting on an optimistic [UNKNOWN] repeat rate or a low early CAC is fragile and must be re-run at a pessimistic band

competency_questions.question: What are the honest, pre-committed kill-criteria that stop good money chasing bad, and why set them before launch?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: KILL_CRITERIA states pre-committed thresholds (a CAC ceiling, a payback ceiling, a first-order-margin floor, a spend cap over the learning window) set before spending, and explains that pre-commitment defeats the sunk-cost pull to keep funding a losing campaign

competency_questions.question: What is the go/no-go verdict logic, and what does the viability segment hand to the assortment/launch decision?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GO_NO_GO_VERDICT combines first-order economics, payback, LTV:CAC and break-even feasibility into a conditional go/no-go, VIABILITY_HANDOFF passes the verdict plus the measured-vs-assumed ledger and kill-switches, and HONESTY_LEDGER separates the [FACT] heuristics from the [UNKNOWN] CAC/repeat/return inputs the launch must measure

glossary.definition: Price minus variable cost per unit: landed COGS + payment-processing fee + pick-pack + variable outbound shipping + expected per-order return cost [FACT-managerial accounting]. Per order it scales with AOV and units-per-order. It is the dollar each order contributes to cover CAC, fixed costs and profit; the number CAC is compared against. Fixed costs and platform subscriptions are excluded here and enter break-even instead.

Acquisition spend divided by NEW customers acquired: paid CAC = paid media spend / new customers from paid; blended CAC = all sales+marketing spend / all new customers. For paid social, CAC = CPM/1000 x impressions / (impressions x CTR x landing-page CVR x new-customer share). The actual value is [UNKNOWN until measured]; category benchmarks are [ESTIMATE] only, and platform-reported CAC understates true CAC post-ATT.

The gross-margin a customer delivers over their relationship = contribution-per-order x expected number of orders per customer, discounted for time and survival [FACT-method]. It must be built on contribution (not revenue) and on a measured or honestly-banded repeat rate; a revenue-times-a-multiple LTV is a fabrication for a low-repeat impulse category and is rejected.

Contribution LTV divided by (marginal paid) CAC. A >=3:1 screening band is a widely-cited venture/SaaS rule of thumb [FACT-heuristic, with caveats], meaning acquisition spend returns ~3x its cost in gross margin. For impulse accessories the ratio is fragile: it silently depends on an [UNKNOWN] repeat rate, so it never stands alone and is always paired with first-order economics and payback.

The time (or number of orders) to recover CAC out of contribution: payback = CAC / contribution-per-period, or orders-to-recover = CAC / contribution-per-order [FACT-method]. A <~12-month or recover-in-first-order-or-two band is the bootstrapped-DTC screen; payback governs the working-capital cash cycle a self-funded launch survives on and often binds tighter than the LTV:CAC ratio.

Contribution-per-order minus CAC on the very first purchase. Positive first-order economics means the business funds its own growth from order one; negative means it is pre-paying for an [UNKNOWN] repeat rate. For a low-repeat impulse accessory, first-order economics is the load-bearing test because the repeat tail is the least certain input.

Break-even units = fixed+launch costs / contribution-per-unit [FACT-CVP]. Break-even ROAS ~= 1 / contribution-margin-ratio: the revenue-per-ad-dollar at which paid spend exactly covers the variable cost of the goods it sells; below it, every incremental ad dollar loses money [FACT-method]. MER (marketing efficiency ratio = total revenue / total ad spend) is the blended, attribution-proof version of the same test.

Blended CAC mixes organic (free) and paid customers and so understates the true cost of the next acquired customer; marginal paid CAC is the cost of the next customer bought with the next ad dollar and is what scaling decisions must use [FACT]. Platform-attributed CAC (Meta/TikTok reported) sits below true paid CAC because ATT/iOS attribution loss over-credits and under-counts; holdout tests and MER correct for it.

Numeric stop-thresholds set BEFORE spending: a CAC ceiling, a payback-period ceiling, a first-order-margin floor, and a total learning-budget cap over a fixed window [METHOD]. Pre-commitment is the honesty device that defeats the sunk-cost fallacy: without it a launch keeps funding a losing campaign hoping the next dollar turns it around. Kill-criteria make the no-go decision automatic and unemotional.

The staged, capped ad spend a launch commits to buy a statistically-usable read on CAC/CVR/AOV per SKU before scaling [METHOD-ESTIMATE]. It is treated as the cost of information (tuition), not as an investment expected to be profitable in-window; its size is set by how many conversions are needed to read CAC with acceptable noise, and it is bounded by the kill-criteria spend cap.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for jewel_economics_viability_cac_ltv work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Accept the per-unit contribution margin as the labelled input this KB runs viability on, without re-deriving it: contribution/unit = retail price (from kb2_pricing_and_margin) - variable cost/unit, where variable cost = landed COGS (from kb1_cogs_and_landed) + payment-processing fee (~2.9%+$0.30 card [FACT-typical published processor pricing, ESTIMATE for the owner's actual rate] ) + pick-pack + variable outbound shipping + expected per-order return cost. Only variable costs enter; platform subscriptions, tooling and fixed overhead are held out for break-even. The inherited price and COGS are [ESTIMATE] bands, so contribution is a band not a point, and its width propagates into every downstream viability number. This is the dollar each order has available to pay CAC, fixed costs and profit.

included: contribution/unit = price - variable cost as accepted input
the variable-cost line items (COGS, processing, pick-pack, shipping, return reserve)
fixed costs held out for break-even
excluded: re-deriving landed COGS (kb1) or retail price/margin construction (kb2)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the inherited price, COGS, processing or shipping rate is updated

pros.claim: Taking price and COGS as labelled inputs keeps the viability model honest about where its uncertainty originates instead of inventing a tighter margin
pros.example: carrying contribution as a band traceable to the [ESTIMATE] COGS and price stops a false-precise single margin driving the verdict

cons.claim: Inheriting a wide price/COGS band caps how tight any viability number can be, so precision is blocked one layer up
cons.example: no CAC or payback refinement can narrow the verdict while the retail price is still a placeholder band

failure_modes: treating gross margin (price - COGS only) as contribution and omitting processing, shipping and return costs, overstating the dollar available for CAC
folding fixed overhead into contribution and double-counting it at break-even
acceptance_tests: contribution/unit is stated as price minus the full variable-cost list (COGS + processing + pick-pack + shipping + return reserve) with fixed costs held out for break-even, carried as an inherited band
revisit_triggers: kb2 republishes the retail price or kb1 the landed COGS
the payment processor or shipping rate for the owner's store is fixed
the return reserve is measured from real orders

nodes.definition: Estimate average order value and units-per-order for the accessory category and state why they run low. Fashion jewelry is typically a low-ticket, often single-item impulse or gift purchase, so AOV is dominated by one piece plus occasional add-ons; units-per-order and AOV are both [UNKNOWN until measured] for the owner's store [METHOD: read them from the existing store's order history 'mindful of the old stuff', then from launch orders; benchmark ranges only [ESTIMATE, LOW confidence]]. AOV is a lever, not a fixed fact: bundles, sets, stacking, and a free-shipping threshold raise it. Because CAC is charged per ORDER (per customer) while contribution is earned per order, a low AOV directly compresses the contribution available to cover a fixed CAC, which is the core viability squeeze for cheap accessories.

included: AOV and units-per-order as measurable inputs
the [METHOD] to read them from existing + launch order data
AOV as a lever (bundles, sets, threshold)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an AOV or units-per-order read from real orders lands

pros.claim: Reading AOV from real order history rather than assuming a number grounds the whole viability model in first-party data
pros.example: pulling the owner's existing store AOV gives a starting basket estimate no benchmark can substitute

cons.claim: Existing-store AOV may not survive a new assortment or a new paid-social audience, so it is a prior not a guarantee
cons.example: a paid-social cold audience may convert at a lower AOV than the warm existing customers

failure_modes: assuming a benchmark AOV as measured and building the verdict on it
confusing AOV with item price when multi-item baskets or discounts move them apart
acceptance_tests: AOV and units-per-order are stated as [UNKNOWN until measured] with the read-from-order-history [METHOD] and AOV named as a lever raised by bundles/sets/threshold
revisit_triggers: the existing store's order history is pulled and AOV read
the launch generates enough orders to measure AOV
a bundle or free-shipping threshold changes the basket

nodes.definition: Define and instrument CAC for paid IG/TikTok/Meta: CAC = acquisition spend / new customers acquired, decomposed through the auction funnel CPM -> impressions -> CTR -> landing-page conversion rate -> new-customer share, so CAC = (CPM/1000) / (CTR x LP-CVR x new-customer-share). Each factor is measurable and improvable, but the resulting CAC is genuinely [UNKNOWN until measured] for the owner's product and audience; any pre-launch CAC is an [ESTIMATE, LOW] planning band, never a fact. Platform-reported CAC is optimistic after iOS-14.5 ATT (under-attribution + modeled conversions) [FACT-attribution degradation], so the measured denominator must be reconciled to real new-customer counts. This is the single most decision-critical [UNKNOWN] in the whole viability model.

included: CAC = spend / new customers and the CPM->CTR->CVR funnel decomposition
CAC as [UNKNOWN until measured] with benchmarks only [ESTIMATE]
platform-reported CAC optimism post-ATT

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured CAC or a funnel-factor change lands

pros.claim: Decomposing CAC into the funnel makes it a measurable, improvable quantity rather than a single opaque guess
pros.example: a poor CAC traced to a 0.8% LP-CVR points at the landing page, not the whole model

cons.claim: Every funnel factor is [UNKNOWN] pre-launch and interacts, so a pre-launch CAC estimate has wide error bars
cons.example: a CPM and CTR both off by 2x compound into a 4x CAC miss

failure_modes: treating a benchmark or a pre-launch CAC estimate as a measured fact and hard-wiring the verdict to it
reading platform-reported CAC as truth and understating true acquisition cost
acceptance_tests: CAC = spend / new customers with the CPM->CTR->LP-CVR funnel is stated, CAC flagged [UNKNOWN until measured], and platform-reported CAC flagged optimistic post-ATT
revisit_triggers: a live campaign returns measured CPM/CTR/CVR and CAC
attribution windows or ATT/platform reporting change
the landing page or creative materially changes the funnel

nodes.definition: Separate three CAC numbers that get conflated and are routinely used to flatter a verdict: blended CAC (all sales+marketing spend / all new customers, diluted downward by free organic customers), marginal paid CAC (the cost of the NEXT customer bought with the next ad dollar), and platform-attributed CAC (Meta/TikTok reported, biased low by ATT loss and modeled conversions). Scaling decisions must steer on marginal paid CAC; profitability of the whole operation is read on blended CAC and MER (marketing efficiency ratio = total revenue / total ad spend), which is attribution-proof [FACT]. A launch that looks viable on blended CAC (propped up by a warm existing audience or a viral post) can be unviable on the marginal paid CAC that governs growth. Reconcile platform-reported new customers to real order counts before trusting any ratio.

included: blended vs marginal vs platform-attributed CAC definitions and biases
MER as the attribution-proof blended read
steer scaling on marginal paid CAC
excluded: the LTV:CAC ratio that consumes CAC (CAC_LTV_RATIO)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the organic/paid mix or an attribution method changes

pros.claim: Naming the three CACs prevents a blended or platform number from masquerading as the growth-governing marginal cost
pros.example: a $6 blended CAC hiding a $22 marginal paid CAC stops a false 'scale it' decision

cons.claim: Marginal paid CAC is the hardest to isolate cleanly, needing holdouts or geo-tests the launch may be too small to run
cons.example: at low volume the marginal CAC read is noisy and may need weeks to stabilize

failure_modes: using blended CAC (diluted by organic) as the denominator for a scaling decision
trusting platform-attributed CAC without reconciling to real new-customer counts
acceptance_tests: blended, marginal paid, and platform-attributed CAC are distinguished with their biases, MER named as the attribution-proof read, and scaling decisions assigned to marginal paid CAC
revisit_triggers: organic share of new customers shifts materially
a holdout/geo-test isolates marginal CAC
platform attribution methodology changes

nodes.definition: Compose contribution-per-order from the inherited unit contribution and the accessory basket: contribution-per-order = (contribution/unit x units-per-order) - order-level variable costs charged once per order (the fixed part of pick-pack, the flat shipping subsidy, the payment fixed fee ~$0.30). This is the exact dollar figure CAC is compared against on every downstream test (first-order economics, payback, LTV, break-even ROAS). Because both contribution/unit and AOV are inherited bands, contribution-per-order is a band; its central value is a [DOWNGRADED] planning anchor, robust in direction, soft in level. For a single-item low-AOV accessory order it is small, which is precisely why CAC discipline is existential here.

included: contribution-per-order = unit contribution x units-per-order minus once-per-order variable costs
it as the denominator/target for CAC, payback and break-even
band-not-point discipline on the figure
excluded: the CAC it is compared against (CAC nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: AOV, unit contribution or order-level cost changes

pros.claim: Computing contribution at the ORDER level matches the unit CAC is charged at, so the first-order comparison is apples-to-apples
pros.example: comparing a $7 contribution-per-order to a $12 CAC immediately exposes a negative first order

cons.claim: Order-level fixed costs (flat shipping, $0.30 fee) hit a low-AOV order hard and are easy to under-count
cons.example: a flat $5 shipping subsidy on a $18 order can halve contribution if mis-modeled

failure_modes: comparing CAC to gross margin per unit instead of contribution per order, understating the true acquisition hurdle
omitting the once-per-order fixed shipping/payment costs that a low-AOV basket cannot dilute
acceptance_tests: contribution-per-order is stated as unit contribution x units-per-order minus once-per-order variable costs, carried as a band, and named as the denominator for CAC/payback/break-even
revisit_triggers: AOV or unit contribution is re-measured
the shipping-subsidy or payment-fee structure changes
a bundle changes units-per-order

nodes.definition: Compute first-order economics = contribution-per-order - CAC on the very first purchase, the load-bearing viability test for a low-repeat impulse category. Positive first-order economics means the launch funds its own growth from order one and the [UNKNOWN] repeat rate is upside, not a dependency; negative means the business is pre-paying to acquire a customer and betting recovery on an unproven repeat tail. Because repeat/LTV is the least certain input for cheap fashion accessories, a model that requires the second order to break even is a model resting on a guess. State the first-order result as a band across the CAC band, and lead the verdict with whether the pessimistic-CAC first order is survivable.

included: first-order profit = contribution-per-order - CAC
why it is load-bearing for a low-repeat category
banding it across the CAC band

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured CAC or contribution-per-order changes the first-order result

pros.claim: Leading with first-order economics removes reliance on the most uncertain input (repeat) for the go decision
pros.example: a positive first order means even zero repeat is not fatal, de-risking the verdict

cons.claim: Insisting on first-order profit can reject a genuinely high-repeat business that legitimately acquires at a first-order loss
cons.example: a subscription-like consumable could rationally lose on order one, though accessories rarely are

failure_modes: declaring viability on a positive LTV while first-order economics is deeply negative and repeat is unproven
using an optimistic early/blended CAC so the first order looks positive when marginal CAC makes it negative
acceptance_tests: first-order profit = contribution-per-order - CAC is computed across the CAC band and the pessimistic-CAC survivability is stated as the lead test
revisit_triggers: a measured CAC narrows the first-order band
contribution-per-order is re-measured
evidence the category is higher-repeat than assumed shifts the reliance

nodes.definition: State honestly that repeat-purchase rate and purchase frequency for fashion accessories are [UNKNOWN until measured] for the owner's brand, and give the method to measure them rather than a number. Fashion jewelry is often a one-off or gift purchase with a long, irregular re-purchase cadence, so a high SaaS-style retention assumption is inappropriate; assume low repeat until data says otherwise [ESTIMATE, LOW]. [METHOD]: build purchase cohorts (customers grouped by first-order month), track the share ordering again at 30/60/90/180/365 days, and read orders-per-customer from the resulting retention curve; the existing store's history ('mindful of the old stuff') is the first cohort source. Never import a repeat rate from another category or invent a retention multiple.

included: repeat/frequency as [UNKNOWN] with a low prior for accessories
the cohort-retention [METHOD]
existing store history as first cohort source

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a maturing cohort yields a measured repeat rate

pros.claim: Refusing to invent a repeat rate and giving a cohort method keeps LTV from resting on a fabricated retention curve
pros.example: an empty 90-day repeat cell honestly reads 'unknown, measure it' rather than a made-up 30%

cons.claim: Cohort repeat data takes months to mature, so early viability must run on a low assumed repeat and be revised
cons.example: a 180-day repeat rate is simply unavailable in week two of a launch

failure_modes: importing a repeat rate from a different category or a benchmark and treating it as the brand's
reading a few early re-orders as a stable repeat rate before the cohort matures
acceptance_tests: repeat/frequency is stated [UNKNOWN until measured] with a low accessory prior and the 30/60/90/180/365-day cohort-retention [METHOD], with existing history named as the first cohort source
revisit_triggers: a purchase cohort matures enough to read a repeat rate
the existing store history is analysed into cohorts
a subscription/replenishment offer changes the repeat structure

nodes.definition: Construct LTV as a contribution (gross-margin) quantity, not a revenue quantity: LTV = contribution-per-order x expected orders-per-customer, discounted for time value and survival, where orders-per-customer comes from the measured/banded repeat curve (REPEAT_RATE_LTV) [FACT-method]. Two disciplines are mandatory: use contribution not revenue (a revenue LTV over a contribution CAC is a category error that overstates value ~3-5x), and use a measured or honestly-pessimistic repeat curve (a revenue-times-arbitrary-multiple LTV is rejected). Report LTV as a band whose width is dominated by the [UNKNOWN] repeat rate; the central figure is a [DOWNGRADED] illustration. LTV feeds the ratio test but never overrides first-order economics for a low-repeat category.

included: LTV = contribution-per-order x discounted orders-per-customer
contribution-not-revenue and measured-repeat disciplines
LTV as a repeat-dominated band
excluded: the ratio and payback that consume LTV (CAC_LTV_RATIO, PAYBACK_PERIOD)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the repeat curve or contribution-per-order updates the LTV band

pros.claim: Building LTV on contribution and a real repeat curve prevents the single most common DTC self-deception (revenue LTV)
pros.example: a $9 contribution LTV replacing a $40 revenue 'LTV' flips a false 3:1 back to a true <1:1

cons.claim: A contribution LTV on an immature repeat curve is a wide band that cannot yet support a confident ratio
cons.example: with only a 30-day repeat read, the orders-per-customer term is a guess with a long tail

failure_modes: computing LTV on revenue instead of contribution and overstating value several-fold
hard-coding an optimistic orders-per-customer before the cohort supports it
acceptance_tests: LTV is stated as contribution-per-order x discounted orders-per-customer on a measured/pessimistic repeat curve, as a band with the central figure flagged [DOWNGRADED]
revisit_triggers: the repeat curve matures and orders-per-customer firms

nodes.definition: Apply the LTV:CAC ratio as a screening band, not a verdict: ratio = contribution LTV / marginal paid CAC, with >=3:1 the widely-cited venture/SaaS rule of thumb [FACT-heuristic, with caveats] and <1:1 an unambiguous fail (you pay more to acquire than the customer ever returns in margin). The caveat is load-bearing for impulse accessories: the ratio inherits the [UNKNOWN] repeat rate through LTV, so a launch can PASS a 3:1 built on an optimistic repeat assumption while FAILING on first-order cash and payback. Therefore the ratio is used to screen out obvious losers and is always reported alongside first-order economics and payback, never as the sole gate. Use marginal paid CAC (not blended) as the denominator so the ratio is not flattered.

included: ratio = contribution LTV / marginal paid CAC with the >=3:1 [FACT-heuristic] band
<1:1 as an unambiguous fail
the repeat-rate fragility caveat

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the LTV band, CAC, or repeat assumption updates the ratio

pros.claim: Using the ratio only as a screen with the marginal-CAC denominator catches obvious losers without over-trusting a single heuristic
pros.example: a <1:1 ratio kills a proposal outright regardless of narrative

cons.claim: The 3:1 rule is a SaaS-origin heuristic that maps poorly onto a low-repeat impulse category and invites false confidence
cons.example: a 3:1 built on an unproven 40% repeat can evaporate to <1:1 when the real repeat is 8%

failure_modes: treating a passing 3:1 as sufficient for a go while first-order economics is negative
computing the ratio on blended CAC and/or revenue LTV, doubly flattering it
acceptance_tests: the ratio is stated as contribution LTV / marginal paid CAC with the >=3:1 screening band and <1:1 fail, the repeat-fragility caveat, and a requirement to pair it with first-order economics and payback
revisit_triggers: the LTV band or marginal CAC updates the ratio
the repeat assumption underlying LTV is measured
a new heuristic band is adopted for the category

nodes.definition: Compute CAC payback = CAC / contribution-per-period, or the simpler orders-to-recover = CAC / contribution-per-order, i.e. how long (or how many orders) until an acquired customer has returned their acquisition cost in gross margin. Screening band: recover within the first order or two, or < ~6-12 months, for a bootstrapped launch [FACT-heuristic]. Payback often binds tighter than the LTV:CAC ratio because it governs the working-capital cash cycle: a self-funded owner must re-fund ad spend before the recovered margin arrives, so a long payback starves growth even when the lifetime ratio looks fine. For a low-repeat category, an orders-to-recover much above ~1 is a red flag because the later orders are the [UNKNOWN] ones.

included: payback = CAC / contribution-per-period and orders-to-recover = CAC / contribution-per-order
the recover-in-1-2-orders / <~12-month band
payback as the cash-cycle governor
excluded: the working-capital funding of inventory (kb1 owns inventory cash)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured CAC, contribution or repeat curve updates payback

pros.claim: Payback surfaces the cash-cycle constraint a bootstrapped DTC actually dies on, which the lifetime ratio hides
pros.example: a 3:1 LTV:CAC with a 10-order payback still starves a self-funded owner of ad cash

cons.claim: Orders-to-recover depends on the same [UNKNOWN] repeat curve, so a multi-order payback is itself uncertain
cons.example: an orders-to-recover of 2 assumes the second order happens, which is the unproven part

failure_modes: reporting a passing lifetime ratio while ignoring a payback longer than the owner can cash-fund
computing payback on optimistic contribution or blended CAC and understating the recovery time
acceptance_tests: payback = CAC / contribution-per-period and orders-to-recover are stated with the recover-in-1-2-orders / <~12-month band and payback named as the cash-cycle governor
revisit_triggers: a measured CAC or contribution updates payback
the repeat curve firms the multi-order recovery
the owner's ad-cash runway changes the acceptable payback

nodes.definition: Derive break-even from the cost+price stack using cost-volume-profit: break-even units = (fixed + one-time launch costs) / contribution-per-unit [FACT-CVP], where fixed costs are the platform subscriptions, tooling, and any salary/overhead held out of contribution, and launch costs include the pre-committed learning budget. Two break-evens matter: contribution break-even (covers fixed costs, ignores CAC) and CAC-inclusive break-even (each unit must also cover its acquisition cost, so the effective contribution is contribution-per-unit - CAC-per-unit; if that is <=0 there is NO break-even volume at that CAC and the model fails regardless of scale). State break-even as a band across the contribution and CAC bands, and flag when no positive-margin volume exists.

included: break-even units = fixed+launch / contribution-per-unit
contribution break-even vs CAC-inclusive break-even
the no-break-even-exists failure when CAC>=contribution

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: fixed cost, contribution or CAC changes the break-even

pros.claim: Computing the CAC-inclusive break-even exposes the fatal case where more volume only deepens the loss
pros.example: a $12 CAC on an $8 contribution has no break-even volume, killing 'we'll make it up on scale'

cons.claim: Break-even units depend on inherited fixed-cost and CAC bands, so the figure is a band not a target headcount
cons.example: an undecided platform/tooling fixed cost swings the contribution break-even materially

failure_modes: computing only the contribution break-even and omitting CAC, hiding a model with no profitable volume
assuming scale fixes a per-unit loss when CAC exceeds contribution
acceptance_tests: break-even units = fixed+launch / contribution-per-unit is stated with both the contribution and CAC-inclusive forms and the explicit no-break-even-exists case when CAC>=contribution
revisit_triggers: fixed or launch costs are fixed at a real number
contribution-per-unit or CAC is re-measured
a subscription/tooling cost is added or removed

nodes.definition: Express the acquisition hurdle as a break-even ROAS/MER the owner can watch in the ad dashboard: break-even ROAS ~= 1 / contribution-margin-ratio, i.e. the revenue-per-ad-dollar at which paid spend exactly covers the variable cost of the goods it sells; below it every incremental ad dollar loses money [FACT-method]. Example structure (not a measured value): a 40% contribution-margin ratio implies a ~2.5x break-even ROAS. MER (marketing efficiency ratio = total revenue / total ad spend) is the blended, attribution-proof twin used for whole-account profitability. Break-even ROAS translates the abstract CAC test into a live guardrail: campaigns below break-even ROAS are cut, campaigns above it can scale until marginal CAC erodes the margin.

included: break-even ROAS ~= 1 / contribution-margin-ratio
MER as the attribution-proof blended twin
ROAS as a live campaign guardrail

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the contribution ratio or attribution gap changes break-even ROAS

pros.claim: Break-even ROAS converts the CAC math into a single dashboard number the owner can act on daily
pros.example: a 2.5x break-even ROAS lets the owner cut any ad set below 2.5x without re-deriving contribution

cons.claim: Platform ROAS is attribution-biased high post-ATT, so a campaign clearing break-even ROAS on-platform may lose on MER
cons.example: a reported 3x ROAS can be a real 2x once ATT over-attribution is removed

failure_modes: steering only on platform-reported ROAS and ignoring the attribution-proof MER
setting break-even ROAS from gross margin instead of contribution margin, understating the true hurdle
acceptance_tests: break-even ROAS ~= 1 / contribution-margin-ratio and MER are stated with ROAS as a live guardrail and the platform-ROAS attribution caveat
revisit_triggers: contribution-margin ratio changes the break-even ROAS
platform attribution shifts the reported-vs-MER gap
a target ROAS bid strategy is adopted

nodes.definition: Model returns, refunds and chargebacks as a deduction from contribution, not an afterthought: net-of-returns contribution = contribution x (1 - return-rate) - per-return handling/restocking/lost-shipping cost. The accessory return rate is [UNKNOWN until measured] for the owner's brand [METHOD: track returns by SKU and reason code from real orders; hygiene rules (pierced earrings often final-sale) and sizing-driven returns are category-specific]. Chargebacks and fraud add a small further drag [FACT-payments]. Returns also destroy the CAC already spent (a returned first order both refunds contribution and forfeits the acquisition cost), so a high return rate compounds directly onto CAC. Carry the return reserve consistently: it is deducted once, inside contribution (CONTRIBUTION_INPUT), never double-counted here and there.

included: net-of-returns contribution = contribution x (1-return-rate) - per-return cost
return rate [UNKNOWN] with a SKU/reason-code [METHOD]
returns forfeiting spent CAC and compounding onto it

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured return, chargeback or policy change occurs

pros.claim: Treating returns as a contribution deduction and a CAC forfeiture prevents a launch that looks viable gross from failing net
pros.example: a 20% return rate on a thin-margin accessory can flip a positive first order negative

cons.claim: The return rate is [UNKNOWN] early, so the drag is an assumed band until real return data accrues
cons.example: a hygiene-driven earring policy may make actual returns far lower than a benchmark

failure_modes: ignoring that a returned order also forfeits the CAC already spent to acquire it
double-counting the return reserve both inside contribution and again as a separate deduction
acceptance_tests: net-of-returns contribution is stated with the [UNKNOWN] return rate + SKU/reason-code [METHOD], the CAC-forfeiture-on-return point, and the reserve carried once inside contribution
revisit_triggers: real return rates by SKU/reason accrue
the return/hygiene policy changes (final-sale on pierced items)
chargeback/fraud rates shift

nodes.definition: Model the free-shipping decision as a contribution-vs-AOV trade: absorbing shipping on a low-AOV accessory order is a direct contribution leak (a flat $4-6 outbound cost is a large share of a sub-$20 order), while a free-shipping threshold set just above current AOV nudges basket size up (add-a-second-item) but only converts if the threshold is reachable with the assortment [METHOD]. Options: charge shipping (protects contribution, may dent conversion), free shipping baked into price (higher sticker, cleaner checkout), or threshold (lifts AOV if tuned). The right choice is [UNKNOWN until tested] and interacts with AOV and returns. State it as a lever the launch A/B-tests, not a fixed policy, and ensure the chosen shipping treatment is reflected consistently in CONTRIBUTION_PER_ORDER.

included: free-shipping vs threshold vs charge as a contribution/AOV trade
threshold-just-above-AOV to lift baskets
shipping treatment reflected consistently in contribution

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a shipping A/B result or a rate change occurs

pros.claim: Framing shipping as a contribution lever tied to AOV stops a reflexive free-shipping giveaway from silently eating the margin
pros.example: a $5 shipping subsidy on a $16 order is a ~30% contribution hit unless a threshold lifts the basket

cons.claim: A threshold set too high suppresses conversion while one too low gives away shipping for free, and the sweet spot is [UNKNOWN] pre-test
cons.example: a $50 threshold on a $18-AOV accessory store may just lower conversion

failure_modes: offering unconditional free shipping on low-AOV orders and leaking contribution
modeling shipping treatment in the threshold node but forgetting to reflect it in contribution-per-order
acceptance_tests: the free-shipping/threshold/charge options are stated as a contribution-vs-AOV trade to be A/B-tested, with the chosen treatment reflected consistently in contribution-per-order
revisit_triggers: an A/B test reads the conversion/AOV effect of a threshold
outbound shipping rates change
the assortment changes what baskets are reachable

nodes.definition: Sequence the launch ad budget as staged experiments with gates, treating the spend as tuition to buy a usable CAC/CVR/AOV read before scaling [METHOD]. Structure: (1) a per-SKU learning budget sized by how many conversions are needed to read CAC with acceptable noise (a handful of conversions is not a CAC); (2) a fixed test window per creative/audience; (3) a gate that only SKUs/audiences clearing break-even ROAS and the first-order test graduate to more spend; (4) a total learning-budget cap tied to the kill-criteria. Do not scale on a few cheap early conversions (the honeymoon/small-sample effect) and do not spread a tiny budget so thin across 6 SKUs that none gets a readable signal. The budget plan is the concrete artifact handed to the launch/assortment decision.

included: staged per-SKU learning budget with test windows and scaling gates
learning spend as tuition, capped by kill-criteria
not scaling on small samples, not spreading budget too thin
excluded: the rising marginal CAC at scale (COHORT_SCALING_CAC_CURVE)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a test window result or an ad-cash change alters the plan

pros.claim: Staging budget with graduation gates buys a statistically-usable read before committing scale spend
pros.example: a per-SKU learning budget yielding ~30-50 conversions reads CAC far better than 3 conversions

cons.claim: A learning budget large enough to read CAC per SKU across 6 SKUs can exceed a bootstrapped owner's cash, forcing fewer test SKUs
cons.example: reading CAC on all 6 SKUs at once may be unaffordable, so tests must be sequenced

failure_modes: scaling spend on a few cheap early conversions before the sample is readable
spreading a small budget so thin across SKUs that no SKU gets a decision-grade signal
acceptance_tests: the staged per-SKU learning budget, test windows, break-even-ROAS graduation gate and kill-criteria-capped total are stated, with the small-sample and thin-spread failure modes guarded
revisit_triggers: a test window closes with a readable CAC/CVR
the owner's available ad cash changes the test scope
a SKU graduates or fails its gate

nodes.definition: State that marginal CAC rises as paid spend scales, so an early cheap CAC does not extrapolate: as budget grows the algorithm exhausts the cheapest, most-responsive audience first and must reach broader, colder users, raising CPM and lowering CVR, so the marginal cost of the next customer climbs (diminishing returns) [FACT-auction economics]. Practical consequence: the CAC read at a small learning budget is a floor, not the scaled CAC; the viability verdict must be tested against the CAC at the intended SCALE budget, not the honeymoon CAC. Model the CAC-vs-spend curve as increasing and re-read CAC at each budget step; a launch viable at $20/day can be unviable at $200/day. This is why launch-budget sequencing gates every scale-up on a fresh CAC read.

included: marginal CAC rising with spend via audience saturation and CPM climb
early CAC as a floor not the scaled CAC
re-reading CAC at each budget step

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a budget-step CAC read or a market CPM shift occurs

pros.claim: Modeling CAC as rising with spend prevents extrapolating a cheap honeymoon CAC into a false scaled verdict
pros.example: a $6 CAC at $20/day becoming $18 at $200/day flips a go into a no-go at scale

cons.claim: The CAC-vs-spend curve is itself [UNKNOWN] until spend is actually scaled, so the scaled CAC is an estimate until tested
cons.example: the exact budget where CAC breaks the break-even line can only be found by stepping spend up

failure_modes: extrapolating the small-budget CAC to the scale budget and declaring viability on the honeymoon rate
scaling in one jump instead of stepping and re-reading CAC
acceptance_tests: marginal CAC is stated as rising with spend (saturation + CPM), the early CAC labelled a floor, and a re-read-CAC-at-each-budget-step rule given
revisit_triggers: a budget step returns a higher measured marginal CAC
audience size or CPM in the market shifts
a new audience/creative resets the curve

nodes.definition: Rank which input the viability verdict is most fragile to and stress-test it before committing. The verdict is a function of CAC, repeat rate, AOV and return rate; for a low-repeat impulse accessory the two most fragile inputs are the marginal-scaled CAC and the [UNKNOWN] repeat rate, because both are unmeasured pre-launch and both swing the verdict across its sign. [METHOD]: re-run first-order economics, payback and the ratio at a pessimistic band for each input (high CAC, low repeat, low AOV, high returns) and see whether the verdict survives; a go that only holds at optimistic inputs is a fragile go. Report the break-point value of each input (the CAC at which first-order economics goes negative, the repeat rate at which LTV:CAC drops below 1) so the launch knows exactly what it must beat.

included: ranking verdict fragility across CAC/repeat/AOV/returns
re-running the tests at pessimistic bands
reporting each input's break-point value

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a measured input narrows a break-point or shifts the binding input

pros.claim: Reporting break-point values turns a vague 'it's risky' into the exact CAC and repeat rate the launch must beat
pros.example: 'first-order economics goes negative above a $9 CAC' is directly actionable in the ad dashboard

cons.claim: A full sensitivity sweep needs several uncertain inputs banded at once, so the stressed verdict is itself a range not a point
cons.example: simultaneous worst-case CAC and repeat may be overly pessimistic and reject a workable launch

failure_modes: reporting only the central-case verdict and hiding that it collapses under a plausible pessimistic input
stressing one input at a time and missing that CAC and repeat degrade together
acceptance_tests: the verdict is re-run at pessimistic CAC/repeat/AOV/return bands and each input's break-point value is reported so the launch knows the thresholds it must beat
revisit_triggers: any input (CAC, repeat, AOV, returns) is measured and narrows the sensitivity
the verdict's binding input changes
a break-point is crossed in live data

nodes.definition: Set honest, numeric kill-criteria BEFORE spending, so the no-go decision is automatic and unemotional: a CAC ceiling (kill a SKU/audience whose measured marginal CAC exceeds the value at which first-order economics goes negative), a payback ceiling (kill if orders-to-recover exceeds the cash-cycle limit), a first-order-margin floor (kill if the pessimistic first order is negative and repeat is unproven), and a total learning-budget spend cap over a fixed window (stop the whole test if the account has not cleared break-even ROAS by cap) [METHOD]. Pre-commitment is the honesty device that defeats the sunk-cost fallacy: without stated thresholds a launch keeps funding a losing campaign hoping the next dollar reverses it. Kill-criteria are the launch's stop-loss and must be written down and agreed before the first ad dollar.

included: pre-committed CAC ceiling, payback ceiling, first-order-margin floor, spend cap
pre-commitment as the anti-sunk-cost device
kill-criteria as the launch stop-loss
excluded: the sensitivity break-points that inform the ceilings (SENSITIVITY_STRESS)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a break-point, cash runway or live threshold hit updates the kill-criteria

pros.claim: Pre-committed numeric kill-criteria stop good money chasing bad by removing the in-the-moment sunk-cost temptation
pros.example: a written $9 CAC ceiling forces a cut a hopeful operator would otherwise keep funding

cons.claim: Thresholds set too tight kill a campaign before its learning sample matures, discarding a workable SKU
cons.example: a hard CAC ceiling hit on day 2 may reflect noise, not the true CAC

failure_modes: setting kill-criteria after spending starts, so sunk cost bends the thresholds
killing on a pre-significance small sample and discarding a viable SKU
acceptance_tests: a CAC ceiling, payback ceiling, first-order-margin floor and windowed spend cap are stated as pre-committed numeric thresholds set before spend, with the sunk-cost rationale and the too-tight/too-early guard
revisit_triggers: a sensitivity break-point revises a ceiling
the owner's cash runway changes the spend cap
a threshold is hit in live data

nodes.definition: Compose the go/no-go verdict from the tests in priority order, not from any single metric: (1) first-order economics at the pessimistic marginal CAC must be survivable, or repeat must be measured (not assumed) high enough to fund the loss; (2) CAC payback must fit the cash cycle; (3) LTV:CAC must clear the screen on contribution/marginal-CAC and not be <1:1; (4) a CAC-inclusive break-even volume must exist and be reachable. The verdict is CONDITIONAL and staged: a 'conditional go' means launch the capped learning test with kill-criteria armed, then a 'scale go' only after the scaled-CAC read clears the gates; a 'no-go' means no positive-margin volume exists at the achievable CAC. State the verdict as a decision procedure over measured-or-banded inputs, always with the [UNKNOWN]s that could flip it named.

included: the priority-ordered go/no-go logic (first-order -> payback -> ratio -> break-even)
conditional/staged go vs scale go vs no-go
verdict as a procedure over measured/banded inputs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a gating input, stage gate or kill-criterion changes the verdict

pros.claim: A priority-ordered conditional verdict prevents a single flattering metric from carrying a go and keeps the decision staged and reversible
pros.example: a passing LTV:CAC cannot force a go while first-order economics fails at marginal CAC

cons.claim: A conditional/staged verdict is less satisfying than a yes/no and demands discipline to re-gate at each stage
cons.example: an owner wanting a clean 'yes' may over-read a conditional go as a full green light

failure_modes: issuing an unconditional go on optimistic inputs without arming kill-criteria or staging the scale read
letting one passing metric (a 3:1 ratio) override a failing higher-priority test (negative first order)
acceptance_tests: the verdict is stated as the priority-ordered first-order -> payback -> ratio -> break-even logic yielding conditional-go / scale-go / no-go, with the flipping [UNKNOWN]s named and kill-criteria armed on any go
revisit_triggers: any gating input is measured and moves the verdict
a stage gate (learning -> scale) is reached
a kill-criterion fires

nodes.definition: Maintain the ledger that keeps the viability model trustworthy in direction without over-reading its level: separate the [FACT] anchors (the contribution/CAC/LTV/payback/break-even formulas, the >=3:1 and <~12-month heuristics as heuristics, the ATT attribution-degradation fact, the rising-marginal-CAC economics) from the [ESTIMATE] planning bands (pre-launch CAC, AOV, benchmark repeat) and the genuine [UNKNOWN]s the launch must measure (actual marginal-scaled CAC, brand repeat rate, return rate). Flag every single-point figure (a CAC, an LTV, a payback) as a [DOWNGRADED] band-centre illustration, robust in direction, soft in level. The ledger is what lets the verdict be acted on as a decision procedure while refusing to quote any acquisition or repeat number as measured before it is.

included: separating [FACT] formulas/heuristics from [ESTIMATE] bands and [UNKNOWN] inputs
flagging single-point figures as [DOWNGRADED] illustrations
the ledger as the trust-in-direction device

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an input graduates label or a heuristic is revised

pros.claim: The ledger lets the model be used for decisions while refusing to launder an assumption into a measured number
pros.example: labelling the pre-launch CAC an [ESTIMATE] band stops it circulating downstream as a fact

cons.claim: A ledger that flags everything as a band can feel like it says nothing firm, tempting stakeholders to ignore it
cons.example: an owner may want a single CAC number and dismiss the honest band as unhelpful

failure_modes: letting an [ESTIMATE] CAC or repeat rate harden into a quoted fact downstream
flagging the heuristics as facts (3:1 is a rule of thumb, not a law) or the formulas as unknowns
acceptance_tests: the ledger separates [FACT] formulas/heuristics from [ESTIMATE] bands and [UNKNOWN] launch-measured inputs, with single-point figures flagged [DOWNGRADED] illustrations
revisit_triggers: an [UNKNOWN] input is measured and graduates to [ESTIMATE]/[FACT]
a heuristic band is revised
a downstream doc is found quoting a band as a fact

nodes.definition: Compose the output this segment hands to the assortment/launch decision: the conditional go/no-go verdict, the staged learning-then-scale budget plan, the armed kill-criteria (CAC/payback/first-order/spend-cap thresholds), the break-point values the launch must beat, and the measured-vs-assumed honesty ledger naming every [UNKNOWN] the launch must measure (marginal-scaled CAC, repeat rate, AOV, return rate). It stops cleanly BEFORE selecting the 6 SKUs (jewel_assortment owns that) and before re-deriving cost/price (kb1/kb2 own those): it delivers whether and under what conditions a paid-social launch is viable, plus the experiment that will replace the [UNKNOWN]s with data. The handoff is a decision procedure plus a measurement plan, never a promised profit number.

included: the verdict + budget plan + armed kill-criteria + break-points + honesty ledger as the output
the clean boundary before SKU selection and cost/price re-derivation
the handoff as decision-procedure-plus-measurement-plan

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a gating input or stage gate changes the handoff

pros.claim: Handing off a conditional verdict plus a measurement plan lets the next stage act while the [UNKNOWN]s get measured, not guessed
pros.example: passing a 'conditional go with a $9 CAC ceiling and a repeat-measurement plan' is actionable and honest

cons.claim: A conditional, band-heavy handoff pushes real decision weight onto the launch measurements, which take time to read
cons.example: the scale-go cannot be given until the scaled-CAC read lands weeks in

failure_modes: handing off a single profit number instead of the conditional verdict, budget plan and measurement plan
letting the handoff drift into selecting SKUs or re-deriving price, overstepping the segment boundary

revisit_triggers: a gating input is measured and updates the verdict/plan

conflict_axes.name: first_order_profit_vs_ltv_bet
conflict_axes.description: First-order economics wants profit on order one, while an LTV narrative argues to acquire at a first-order loss and recover on repeat; for a low-repeat accessory the repeat tail is the least certain input.
poles: acquire at a loss and recover on LTV
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: lead with first-order economics; allow a first-order loss only when the repeat rate is measured (not assumed) high enough to fund it

conflict_axes.name: blended_flattery_vs_marginal_truth
conflict_axes.description: Blended CAC (diluted by organic) and platform-attributed CAC look attractive, while the marginal paid CAC that actually governs scaling is higher.
poles: steer on the true marginal paid CAC
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use marginal paid CAC and MER for scaling and profitability; treat blended/attributed CAC as context, never as the scaling denominator

conflict_axes.name: ratio_screen_vs_payback_cash
conflict_axes.description: A healthy lifetime LTV:CAC ratio can coexist with a payback so long it starves a self-funded owner of ad cash.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat payback as the binding constraint for a bootstrapped launch; a passing ratio with an unfundable payback is still a no-go

conflict_axes.name: honeymoon_cac_vs_scaled_cac
conflict_axes.description: The cheap CAC read at a small learning budget tempts extrapolation, while marginal CAC rises as spend scales into colder audiences.
poles: verdict on the scaled marginal CAC
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the early CAC as a floor; re-read CAC at each budget step and gate the scale-go on the scaled CAC, not the honeymoon rate

conflict_axes.name: learn_more_vs_kill_now
conflict_axes.description: More ad spend always promises a cleaner read, while a pre-committed cap says stop a test that has not cleared its gates.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: honor the pre-committed spend cap and kill thresholds; extending the test past the cap needs explicit written re-authorization, not sunk-cost drift

conflict_axes.name: single_number_vs_honest_band
conflict_axes.description: Stakeholders want one CAC, one LTV, one payback, while the evidence supports only bands dominated by [UNKNOWN] CAC and repeat.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: carry the band and flag any single-point figure a [DOWNGRADED] illustration robust in direction and soft in level

conflict_axes.name: revenue_ltv_vs_contribution_ltv
conflict_axes.description: A revenue-based LTV inflates value several-fold over the contribution-based LTV that can honestly be compared to CAC.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always build LTV on contribution and a measured repeat curve; a revenue LTV over a contribution CAC is a category error and is rejected

conflict_axes.name: free_shipping_conversion_vs_contribution
conflict_axes.description: Free shipping lifts conversion but leaks contribution on a low-AOV order, while charging or a threshold protects contribution but may dent conversion.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: A/B-test a threshold set just above AOV; do not offer unconditional free shipping on sub-threshold low-AOV orders

conflict_axes.name: scale_volume_vs_no_break_even
conflict_axes.description: Scaling volume is assumed to fix losses, but if CAC exceeds contribution there is NO break-even volume and more scale only deepens the loss.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: compute the CAC-inclusive break-even first; if per-unit margin after CAC is <=0, stop scaling and fix CAC or contribution before spending

edge_cases.description: A revenue-based LTV is compared to a contribution-based CAC, producing a false 3:1 that is really <1:1
edge_cases.trigger: LTV computed on revenue while CAC is a cash cost
edge_cases.mitigation: rebuild LTV on contribution-per-order x measured orders-per-customer and re-run the ratio

edge_cases.description: The launch scales spend on a cheap honeymoon CAC read from a handful of early conversions and CAC triples at scale
edge_cases.trigger: extrapolating a small-sample early CAC to the scale budget
edge_cases.mitigation: treat early CAC as a floor, re-read CAC at each budget step, and gate the scale-go on the scaled marginal CAC

edge_cases.description: First-order economics is deeply negative but a passing LTV:CAC on an ASSUMED repeat rate is used to declare a go
edge_cases.trigger: an optimistic unmeasured repeat rate carries the verdict
edge_cases.mitigation: require positive pessimistic-CAC first-order economics unless repeat is measured; do not fund a first-order loss on a guess

edge_cases.description: CAC exceeds contribution so no positive-margin volume exists, yet the plan proposes to 'make it up on scale'
edge_cases.trigger: per-unit margin after CAC is <=0 and scale is invoked as the fix
edge_cases.mitigation: recognize there is no break-even volume; fix CAC or contribution before any scale spend

edge_cases.description: Blended CAC (propped up by a warm existing audience or a viral post) is used to justify scaling paid spend
edge_cases.trigger: a scaling decision made on blended not marginal CAC
edge_cases.mitigation: isolate marginal paid CAC (holdout/step-up) and steer scaling on it; use blended/MER only for whole-account profit

edge_cases.description: A returned first order both refunds contribution and forfeits the CAC, and the model counted neither
edge_cases.trigger: returns modeled as a minor cost, ignoring the forfeited acquisition spend
edge_cases.mitigation: deduct net-of-returns contribution and treat a returned first order as lost CAC plus refunded contribution

edge_cases.description: The lifetime LTV:CAC ratio passes but the payback is far longer than the owner can cash-fund ad spend
edge_cases.trigger: a long payback hidden behind a healthy lifetime ratio
edge_cases.mitigation: make payback the binding constraint for the bootstrapped launch; a passing ratio with an unfundable payback is a no-go

edge_cases.description: Unconditional free shipping is offered on sub-$20 orders, leaking a large share of contribution
edge_cases.trigger: a free-shipping giveaway on low-AOV baskets with no threshold
edge_cases.mitigation: set and A/B-test a free-shipping threshold just above AOV, or bake shipping into price

edge_cases.description: Kill-criteria are set after spending begins, so sunk cost bends the thresholds and a losing campaign keeps running
edge_cases.trigger: thresholds defined post-launch under sunk-cost pressure
edge_cases.mitigation: write and agree numeric kill-criteria before the first ad dollar and enforce them automatically

edge_cases.description: A pre-launch CAC or repeat rate estimate circulates downstream as if it were a measured fact
edge_cases.trigger: an [ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] input quoted without its tag
edge_cases.mitigation: carry the honesty ledger; label pre-launch CAC/repeat as [ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] bands and single points as [DOWNGRADED]

edge_cases.description: A tiny total budget is spread across all 6 SKUs so none reaches a decision-grade CAC signal
edge_cases.trigger: under-powered per-SKU spend from over-splitting a small budget
edge_cases.mitigation: sequence tests to fund fewer SKUs to a readable sample rather than starving all six

edge_cases.description: Platform-reported ROAS clears break-even while the attribution-proof MER shows the account losing money
edge_cases.trigger: steering on platform ROAS inflated by ATT over-attribution
edge_cases.mitigation: cross-check platform ROAS against MER (total revenue / total ad spend) and steer on the attribution-proof number

workflow.description: State contribution/unit = price - full variable cost (COGS + processing + pick-pack + shipping + return reserve), fixed costs held out, as an inherited band
workflow.gate: contribution/unit is stated with the full variable-cost list and fixed costs held out for break-even

workflow.description: Read AOV and units-per-order from existing + launch order data as [UNKNOWN until measured] with the read-from-history method
workflow.gate: AOV and units-per-order are stated [UNKNOWN] with a method and AOV named as a lever

workflow.description: Define CAC = spend / new customers via the CPM->CTR->LP-CVR funnel, flag it [UNKNOWN] and platform CAC optimistic post-ATT
workflow.gate: CAC funnel is stated with CAC flagged [UNKNOWN until measured] and the ATT caveat

workflow.description: Separate blended, marginal paid and platform-attributed CAC and assign scaling decisions to marginal paid CAC and MER
workflow.gate: the three CACs and MER are distinguished and scaling is assigned to marginal paid CAC

workflow.action: Compose contribution-per-order and the first-order test
workflow.description: Build contribution-per-order then first-order profit = contribution-per-order - CAC across the CAC band
workflow.gate: first-order profit is computed across the CAC band with pessimistic-CAC survivability stated

workflow.action: Build the contribution LTV on a measured repeat curve
workflow.description: Measure repeat via cohorts, then LTV = contribution-per-order x discounted orders-per-customer, as a repeat-dominated band
workflow.gate: LTV is built on contribution and a measured/pessimistic repeat curve, central figure flagged [DOWNGRADED]

workflow.action: Apply the ratio and payback screens
workflow.description: Compute LTV:CAC on marginal CAC and CAC payback / orders-to-recover, with payback as the cash-cycle governor
workflow.gate: the ratio (>=3:1 screen, <1:1 fail) and payback (recover-in-1-2-orders / <~12mo) are stated with marginal CAC

workflow.action: Derive break-even units and break-even ROAS
workflow.description: Compute break-even units = fixed+launch / contribution-per-unit, the CAC-inclusive form, and break-even ROAS ~= 1/contribution-ratio
workflow.gate: break-even units (both forms, incl. the no-break-even case) and break-even ROAS/MER are stated

workflow.description: Deduct net-of-returns contribution and set the free-shipping-vs-threshold treatment consistently in contribution
workflow.gate: net-of-returns contribution and the shipping treatment are stated and reflected in contribution-per-order

workflow.action: Sequence the launch budget and scaled-CAC curve
workflow.description: Stage a per-SKU learning budget with graduation gates and re-read the rising marginal CAC at each step
workflow.gate: the staged learning budget, graduation gates and re-read-CAC-per-step rule are stated

workflow.description: Report each input's break-point and set pre-committed CAC/payback/first-order/spend-cap kill thresholds before spend
workflow.gate: break-points are reported and pre-committed numeric kill-criteria are set before the first ad dollar

workflow.description: Combine the tests into a conditional go/no-go, package verdict + budget plan + kill-criteria + break-points + honesty ledger, stop before SKU selection
workflow.gate: the conditional verdict, budget plan, armed kill-criteria, break-points and honesty ledger are handed off within the clean boundary

priority_rationale: The inherited unit contribution, accessory AOV and paid-social CAC come first because every viability number is contribution-per-order compared against CAC; the blended-vs-marginal CAC reconciliation and contribution-per-order composition come next because they fix the honest denominator and the value CAC is subtracted from; first-order economics, the contribution LTV on a measured repeat curve, the ratio and payback, and the break-even units/ROAS then apply the tests in the order that matters for a low-repeat bootstrapped launch (first-order cash before lifetime ratio); returns/shipping drag, staged launch budget and the rising scaled-CAC curve add the real-world leaks and the scaling reality; and sensitivity, pre-committed kill-criteria, the conditional go/no-go verdict, the honesty ledger and the handoff come last because they compose, stress, and honestly package the verdict plus the measurement plan that replaces every [UNKNOWN] with launch data.

dominance_rules.rule: First-order economics dominates a favorable LTV for a low-repeat category
dominance_rules.rationale: the repeat tail is the least certain input, so a go resting on it is a go resting on a guess
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposal funds a first-order loss on an assumed repeat rate
dominance_rules.action: require positive pessimistic-CAC first-order economics unless repeat is measured, not assumed

dominance_rules.rule: Marginal paid CAC dominates blended and platform-attributed CAC for scaling
dominance_rules.rationale: blended CAC is diluted by organic and platform CAC is inflated by ATT over-attribution
dominance_rules.trigger: a scaling decision cites blended or platform CAC
dominance_rules.action: recompute on marginal paid CAC and MER before scaling

dominance_rules.rule: Payback dominates the lifetime ratio for a bootstrapped launch
dominance_rules.rationale: the cash cycle, not the lifetime return, is what starves a self-funded owner of ad spend
dominance_rules.trigger: a go rests on a passing ratio with an unfundable payback
dominance_rules.action: treat payback as the binding constraint and no-go the unfundable payback

dominance_rules.rule: The scaled marginal CAC dominates the honeymoon CAC
dominance_rules.rationale: marginal CAC rises with spend as the audience saturates and CPM climbs
dominance_rules.trigger: a scale decision extrapolates the small-budget CAC
dominance_rules.action: re-read CAC at each budget step and verdict the scale-go on the scaled CAC

dominance_rules.rationale: a revenue LTV over a contribution CAC overstates value several-fold and is a category error
dominance_rules.trigger: an LTV is computed on revenue
dominance_rules.action: rebuild LTV on contribution-per-order x measured orders-per-customer

dominance_rules.rationale: pre-commitment defeats the sunk-cost pull to keep funding a losing campaign
dominance_rules.trigger: a campaign past a kill threshold is kept running on hope
dominance_rules.action: enforce the pre-committed thresholds automatically; extension needs written re-authorization

dominance_rules.rule: The CAC-inclusive break-even dominates the contribution-only break-even
dominance_rules.rationale: a model with no positive per-unit margin after CAC has no break-even volume at all
dominance_rules.trigger: only the contribution break-even is computed
dominance_rules.action: compute the CAC-inclusive break-even and stop scaling if per-unit margin after CAC is <=0

dominance_rules.rule: The honest band dominates any single-point figure
dominance_rules.rationale: the [UNKNOWN] CAC and repeat rate make a point CAC/LTV/payback unsupportable pre-launch
dominance_rules.trigger: a single CAC/LTV/payback point is quoted as measured
dominance_rules.action: carry the band and label the point a [DOWNGRADED] illustration

dominance_rules.rule: A measured input dominates its assumption of the same name
dominance_rules.rationale: the whole model exists to replace [UNKNOWN] CAC/repeat/return assumptions with launch data
dominance_rules.trigger: a live measurement contradicts the planning assumption
dominance_rules.action: update the verdict to the measured input and re-gate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute contribution as price minus the FULL variable-cost list (incl. processing, shipping, return reserve) from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a verdict built on gross margin that must be redone once real per-order costs surface

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build LTV on contribution and a measured repeat curve from the start, never on revenue or an assumed multiple
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a revenue-LTV ratio that later collapses below 1:1 and invalidates the whole go decision

anti_rework_rules.rule: Use marginal paid CAC (not blended/attributed) as the scaling denominator from the first analysis
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a scale-up justified on a flattering blended CAC that fails at the marginal CAC governing growth

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat the early learning-budget CAC as a floor and plan to re-read CAC at each budget step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: extrapolating a honeymoon CAC to scale and re-doing the verdict after CAC triples

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write pre-committed numeric kill-criteria before the first ad dollar
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sunk-cost-bent thresholds set mid-flight that let a losing campaign burn the budget

anti_rework_rules.rule: Compute the CAC-inclusive break-even alongside the contribution break-even in the same step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering only after scaling that no positive-margin volume ever existed at the achievable CAC

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every CAC/repeat/return figure [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] and flag single points [DOWNGRADED] on first use
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an assumption circulating downstream as a measured fact and having to be retracted from later docs

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reflect the chosen shipping/returns treatment inside contribution-per-order once, not in separate nodes
anti_rework_rules.prevents: double-counting or omitting the shipping subsidy and return reserve across the model

iteration_protocol.trigger: a live campaign returns a measured CAC (CPM/CTR/CVR)
iteration_protocol.action: replace the [ESTIMATE] CAC band with the measured value and re-run first-order economics, payback, ratio and break-even

iteration_protocol.trigger: a purchase cohort matures enough to read a repeat rate
iteration_protocol.action: update the repeat curve and re-band LTV, the ratio and orders-to-recover payback

iteration_protocol.trigger: a budget step returns a higher scaled marginal CAC
iteration_protocol.action: update the CAC-vs-spend curve, re-check kill-criteria and re-gate the scale-go

iteration_protocol.trigger: AOV or units-per-order is measured from real orders
iteration_protocol.action: recompute contribution-per-order and every downstream test that consumes it

iteration_protocol.trigger: real return/refund/chargeback rates by SKU accrue
iteration_protocol.action: update net-of-returns contribution and re-run the first-order and break-even tests

iteration_protocol.trigger: kb1 landed COGS or kb2 retail price is republished
iteration_protocol.action: update the inherited unit contribution and re-run the whole viability stack

iteration_protocol.trigger: a kill-criterion or stage gate fires in live data
iteration_protocol.action: execute the pre-committed action (cut/hold/scale) and re-issue the conditional verdict and handoff

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
19-24 nodes, 32-40 edges, 8-10 conflict_axes, 10-12 edge_cases, 9-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run
